_comment: Every control map this box can produce, from one input image, in one graph: Depth Anything 3 depth (raw + colourised), MoGe-2 surface normals, and SDPose whole-body pose. These are the inputs that drive controlled composition for both stills (Qwen ControlNet) and video (LTX IC-LoRA). Until now the weights were installed and nothing referenced them.
_notes: Feed the raw `depth` output into a ControlNet or LTX IC-LoRA. The `depth_colored` output is a turbo-colormap VISUALISATION for humans - never feed that to a model, it will read the false colours as content.

DYNAMIC COMBOS BITE TWICE HERE. `DA3Inference.mode` = 'mono' takes no sub-inputs, so a bare string is fine. But `DA3Render.output` = 'depth' DOES take sub-inputs - `output.normalization` and `output.apply_sky_clip` - as dotted keys. Omit them and you get the worst possible failure mode: ComfyUI validates the two DA3 outputs as invalid, **silently drops them, and still reports the prompt as `success`**. You get a green run with two of four images and no error unless you read the server log. Always count your outputs.

normalization: `v2_style` (mean/std, perceptually balanced) is the right default for feeding a ControlNet. `min_max` stretches to full range for maximum contrast - better for the human-readable colourised version, worse as control input because it exaggerates near-field depth. `raw` preserves metric units and is only meaningful on the Metric model.

resolution 504 is DA3's native working size. `upper_bound_resize` fits the long edge (safer, keeps the whole frame); `lower_bound_resize` fits the short edge and crops - use it when the subject is centred and you want maximum detail on it.

MoGe-2 gives NORMALS, which DA3 does not. Normals encode surface orientation rather than distance, so they hold small surface relief - fabric folds, panel lines, carved detail - that depth flattens. `normal_opengl` is the ComfyUI/Blender convention; `normal_directx` flips green for engines that expect it. Getting this backwards inverts your lighting.

Both DA3 and MoGe load through their own loaders but share one model dropdown, so it is easy to pick the wrong file. LoadDA3Model wants `depth_anything_3_mono_large`; LoadMoGeModel wants `moge_2_vitl_normal_fp16`.

SDPose needs a MODEL and a VAE - it is a diffusion-based pose estimator, not a classifier, which is why it is a checkpoint rather than a small detector. It handles ONE person by default; multi-person needs `RTDETR_detect` to supply per-person bboxes, and that detector's weights are not installed.
draw_feet defaults false and is worth turning on for full-body shots - foot orientation is most of what sells a standing pose.
All three maps also work on a video frame batch, which is exactly what the LTX IC-LoRA wants for camera control.
